hints: Notice the four behaviours tested: diffracted, travel in free space, coherent, and polarised.
Recall that in a transverse wave vibrations are perpendicular to energy travel, while in a longitudinal wave vibrations are parallel to energy travel.
Ask yourself which process needs to select one vibration plane out of many, and which processes such as diffraction and interference happen for all wave types.
walkthrough: Identify the vibration directions: transverse vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of travel, longitudinal vibrations are parallel to the direction of travel.
Check diffraction: all waves spread when passing a gap of width similar to wavelength $\lambda$, so it is not limited to longitudinal waves.
Check free space travel: transverse electromagnetic waves can travel in vacuum, while longitudinal sound waves need particles of a medium, so the free-space statement is reversed.
Check coherence: two waves are coherent if they have the same frequency and constant phase difference, which is possible for both sound and light.
Check polarisation: polarising restricts an unpolarised wave with many perpendicular vibration planes to one plane, which only makes sense for a transverse wave.
A longitudinal wave has only one vibration line along travel, so it cannot be polarised. This is option D.

options.A: Diffraction is spreading through a gap or around an obstacle and occurs for all waves, both transverse and longitudinal.
options.B: Electromagnetic waves are transverse and travel in free space, while sound is longitudinal and needs a medium.
options.C: Coherence means constant phase difference and can apply to both transverse light and longitudinal sound sources.
options.D: Polarisation restricts vibrations to one plane, which is only possible when vibrations are perpendicular to travel in a transverse wave.
